fields.acceptance: A testscript drives a headless run (driver with no REX_BLOCK) whose agent session, under a fake rex, blocks on a question and then resumes: the session wrapper's terminal output holds exactly one root-record blocked report with kind=question, app=rhiza, title the tab and msg naming the change set, step and question, then one working report; the driver writes no report; a --foreground run with REX_BLOCK set still writes its notice to its own block as run-blocked.txtar checks
fields.statement: When a run's agent session blocks, its own tab's wrapper (rhiza session run) writes rhiza's root-record OSC 7501 blocked report to its terminal, with the kind, the tab as title and a message naming the change set, the step and the question, and a working report once the block ends, so a headless run's block reaches Rex with no driver, daemon or watcher tab

fields.acceptance: Evidence from the VM after installing the fix: either the owner saw a macOS banner for a question in a VM agent tab, or docs/rex-upstream/notification-banner.md is committed with the Rex versions (Mac app and VM server), the exact OSC 7501 bytes rhiza and Claude Code wrote as captured by rex events --json, the remote VM host setup, the Mac's focus and notification-permission state, and the symptom (chime, no banner), and an inbox item points the owner at it to file with Rex
fields.statement: Once agent-tab-blocked-notice is installed on the VM, a question asked in a VM agent tab is checked on the Mac for a banner, and if it still only chimes a report for Rex upstream is drafted in the repo for the owner to file
